what_its_for: Solifenacin is used to treat overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, frequent urination, and accidental leaks (urge incontinence). It works by relaxing the bladder muscle so your bladder can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day so it becomes part of your routine. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store solifenacin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store it in a dry place, such as a dresser drawer — not in the bathroom medicine cabinet. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid activities that require sharp alertness, like driving or operating heavy machinery, until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or blurred vision. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, because solifenacin reduces sweating and can raise your body temperature. Limit alcohol, as it can increase drowsiness. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, especially antifungals like ketoconazole, as they can increase solifenacin levels in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: difficulty urinating or cannot urinate at all, severe constipation or stomach pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, confusion or memory problems, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in bladder symptoms within 1 to 2 weeks, but it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit of this medication. Be patient and continue taking it as directed even if you do not notice immediate results.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, confusion, and constipation. Use caution and report any new or worsening symptoms to your doctor. Kidney or liver problems: If you have moderate to severe kidney or liver disease, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose. Do not take the 10 mg dose if you have severe kidney or liver problems. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: The safety of solifenacin during pregnancy or breastfeeding is not well established. Talk to your doctor before using this medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
